title: Pressed Leaf — Permaculture Module
description: A course-module slide that feels like a page torn from a botanical field manual: single pressed-leaf illustration, calm humanist serif, and hairline-ruled learning objectives that let the content breathe rather than perform.
philosophy: This template exists for educators who trust their material to carry the room without visual theatrics. It draws from the quiet rigour of botanical-textbook layout and Schumacher College's conviction that learning environments should feel grounded, not stimulated. It refuses gradients, hero imagery, and anything that competes with the text for attention. The design is a container — unobtrusive, warm, and honest about its instructional purpose.
goodFor: Workshop module slides listing 3–5 numbered learning objectives
Permaculture, ecology, or regenerative-design course content
Slides printed as handouts or projected in naturally-lit seminar rooms
Instructors pairing digital slides with physical field notebooks
avoidFor: Venture-capital or investor pitch decks requiring high visual energy
Chart-heavy quarterly reviews with multiple graphs per slide
Large dark-room auditorium presentations needing high contrast
Brand campaigns where visual identity must dominate the layout
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like the inside cover of a well-used botanical field manual — unhurried, warm, and quietly authoritative. A single pressed-leaf illustration occupies the upper-right quadrant with the restraint of a specimen plate, its muted organic tones echoing the linen ground rather than competing with it. Compositionally asymmetric: botanical element breathes in the upper register while the title and subtitle settle into the lower-left with grounded calm. Avoid anything performative — no shadow, no decorative flourish, no spotlight effect; only the honest stillness of instructional purpose.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with generous outer margins (~10% each side) to replicate the breathing quality of a bound field manual. Pressed-leaf illustration is positioned upper-right, spanning roughly half the column width and softened to low opacity so it reads as specimen-plate texture rather than hero art. Course or module label sits as a small tracked-cap string in the upper-left corner; the deck title anchors left in the lower third with the subtitle nested immediately below it, the two separated by a single full-width hairline rule. Bottom margin carries a second hairline spanning the full text column with a date or institution credit at the trailing end — no page number on the title slide.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a careful hand-copied page from a botanical field manual — orderly but warm, purposeful without ornamentation. A single delicate pressed-leaf sits quietly in the right column, not commanding attention but grounding the eye; it functions as margin art, not illustration. Numbered objectives stack with ledger discipline, each bounded above and below by a gossamer rule that gives the list rhythm without weight. The overall mood is hushed seminar room on a grey morning: studious, trustworthy, and completely uninterested in impressing anyone. Avoid any decorative flourish, texture overlay, or element that competes with the text for priority.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-col grid; text block occupies cols 2–8, leaving cols 9–12 for a single small pressed-leaf illustration anchored to the right margin at mid-height. Outer margin ~9% on all sides for a 'torn-page' breathing quality. Module number sits top-left as a small label above a full-width hairline rule that separates the header zone from the body. Each learning objective is a numbered line separated from the next by another hairline rule, creating a ledger-like stacked rhythm. No footer band; page number placed as a bare numeral bottom-right outside the text block.
